text:
Alicia: Heads up — hitting GPU quota limits in Australia East for the inference fleet. Several jobs are failing with allocation errors since this morning. Case opened with MSFT: 21458972.
Kevin: Ugh. Which SKU and limit are we over?
Alicia: Mostly NDv4/A100 and the regional vCPU/vNET interface (ENI-equivalent) soft limits. Error we see: "Allocation failed: No available GPUs in location".
Maria: Can you paste the `az` output?
Alicia: Sure — running `az vm list-usage --location australiaeast --output table` shows:
```
Name                                      CurrentValue  Limit
Standard NC A100 v4 Family vCPUs             96           100
Available GPUs (A100)                          6            6
Network Interface Count                       240         250
```
Alicia: We requested +50 vCPUs and +10 GPUs in the case. MSFT replied asking for business justification and expected sustained usage.
Navin: What's our timeline? Any production impact?
Alicia: Some canary jobs timed out; small % of inference traffic routed to Dedicated pool but latency increased. Not user-visible yet but risk for morning traffic spike.
Kevin: Ok. Short term we should: 1) spill to Japan East for non-sensitive workloads, 2) throttle batch size on aueast for now, 3) ask MSFT for expedited review.
Maria: For spillover, I can spin up 8 instances in Japan East if we get quota there. We have spare capacity in our Reserved pool region.
Alicia: MSFT asked for an exact list of VMs and a capacity curve (monthly token/s). I attached a brief justification in the case but we need numbers.
Kevin: I'll draft numbers. Quick ask: can we temporarily switch some jobs to preemptible/spot to reduce demand?
Navin: Yes for training/test jobs, but not for production inference. We can modify autoscaler to prefer spot for batch.
ops-bot: Incident alert: 3 inference jobs failed in australiaeast between 2025-12-05T02:10Z and 2025-12-05T03:05Z. IDs: inf-job-9821, inf-job-9824, inf-job-9850.
Alicia: MSFT response at 1765503200: "We have assigned this to Azure Capacity Management team. Need a 24-48 hour window. Provide expected sustained vCPU/GPU usage and peak burst windows."
Maria: I'll compile a CSV of hourly usage for the past 7 days and expected peak on Monday.
Kevin: Also request escalation path — ask for an ASM (Account Service Manager) contact or to move it to Priority 2. Case note to add: "Customer running production inference, latency-sensitive, risk of degraded SLOs".
Alicia: Drafted note. Pasting here for review:
```
We are Redwood Inference, running production LLM inference in Australia East. Current fleet needs an immediate quota increase of +10 A100 GPUs and +200 vCPUs to sustain production throughput. Peak windows are weekdays 02:00–06:00 UTC (APAC morning), expected sustained GPU utilization 80% during peaks. Please escalate to Capacity Management and assign ASM for faster review.
```
Navin: 👍 looks good. Add a line about committed spend if that helps (we can commit $X/month for reserved capacity).
Alicia: Done — added committed spend line. Re-submitted to case 21458972 at 1765503600.
ops-bot: Case 21458972 updated: status -> In review by Capacity Management (1765503600).
Maria: If they need immediate relief, I can start shifting non-sensitive traffic to Japan East now. Any objections?
Kevin: Do it. Also create a temporary routing rule in Smart Router to prefer Japan East when Australia East responds with allocation errors. Keep per-request metadata so we can revert.
Alicia: I'll open a PR for the routing change and add a canary (5% traffic) to Japan East first.
Navin: Cost question — Japan East spot rates are ~25% higher for some SKUs. We'll track cost delta in the Console tagging.
Kevin: Add an alert to #finance for expected monthly delta and cc Growth leads.
Alicia: Thanks team. I'll follow up once Capacity Management replies or if we need a formal escalation.
Maria: I'll attach the CSV and usage graphs to the case and DM the ASM contact if they provide one.
Alicia: Final note — if no resolution in 48 hours, we plan to open a support escalation via our Microsoft partner channel. Put that as a fallback in the case.
Kevin: Cool. Keeping thread for updates.
Alicia: Update 1765504799: Capacity Management asked for topology diagram and VNet details — attaching shortly.
